newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linotype sees return to profitabilty in two years.
newsitem.headline: Linotype sees return to profitabilty in two years.

text.p: German printing group Linotype-Hell AG said on Tuesday that it expected to return to profitability in two years.
"We expect that with our new structure we will return to profitability in two years," Linotype management board chairman Bernhard Schreier said in a statement.
Linotype earlier on Tuesday said it expected to report a 1996 operating loss of about 73 million marks at the parent company level and about 82 million marks for the group.
Linotype has announced a major restructuring plan that calls for about 1,200 jobs to be cut and to centralise activities at its Kiel production site.
The printing group was taken over by printing machinery group Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG, which is a subsidiary of Rheinelektra AG.
